battle.name: 尼加拉瓜內戰
battle.brief: 尼加拉瓜內戰自一九六一年十二月起，由桑地諾民族解放陣線對抗索莫莎政府，延續至一九七九年政權更替。此役屬二十世紀中葉拉丁美洲反抗獨裁統治的內戰；英國海軍早於一九六一年已列裝鐵甲艦（Ironclad），代表蒸汽動力裝甲戰艦的海上兵力。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 鐵甲艦是英國皇家海軍早期裝甲蒸汽主力艦，配置於遠洋艦隊，擔任旗艦並執行巡邏、護航及海外駐防，屬當時海軍水面兵力的核心。

countries: 本文把1961年界定為組織化游擊戰的起點，而不是一場具有固定戰場、同日勝負與單一會戰時刻的戰役；公開內戰通常又以1967年算起。地理主線從馬塔爾帕、布奧科與新塞哥維亞的中央山區，延伸至馬薩亞、馬納瓜、里巴斯及北部城鎮。交戰核心是桑迪諾民族解放陣線，對手則是索莫薩政府的國民警衛隊、軍隊與警察。洪都拉斯與哥斯大黎加提供邊境後勤及臨時營地條件，古巴在較後期提供武器與訓練，美國既是國民警衛隊早年的訓練及供應方，也在1970年代後期成為援助與外交政策轉折的關鍵。少數跨境行動主要服務於情報、補給與撤退，不能把這場內戰寫成外國軍隊直接攻入尼加拉瓜。
countriesEn: This account treats 1961 as the beginning of organized guerrilla warfare rather than a single battle with a fixed field, a same-day result, and one decisive moment. The public civil war is more commonly dated from 1967. The geographical axis ran from the central highlands of Matagalpa, Boaco, and Nueva Segovia to Masaya, Managua, Rivas, and towns in the north. The principal opposing forces were the Sandinista National Liberation Front and the Somoza government's National Guard, army, and police. Honduras and Costa Rica provided border logistics and temporary basing conditions, Cuba supplied weapons and training in the later phase, and the United States, having earlier trained and equipped the Guard, became decisive in aid and diplomatic policy in the late 1970s. A small number of cross-border activities served intelligence, supply, and withdrawal; the conflict should not be described as a foreign army directly invading Nicaragua.
people: 桑迪諾民族解放陣線於1961年成立，最初核心包括卡洛斯・方塞卡、西爾維奧・馬約爾加、托馬斯・博爾赫與桑托斯・洛佩斯。方塞卡負責政治方向與游擊戰理論，馬約爾加著重建立山區隊伍，博爾赫整頓指揮及後勤，後來加入的洪伯托・奧爾特加則成為重要軍事指揮者。埃登・帕斯托拉於1967年加入陣線，他曾在桑迪諾將軍麾下作戰，帶來不同於學生出身幹部的實戰經驗。方塞卡於1968年5月陣亡，馬約爾加則在1967年12月空難身亡，使早期指揮一度中斷。索莫薩家族方面，老索莫薩・加西亞自1936年執政至1956年遇刺，路易斯・索莫薩・德拜萊短期接任後，阿納斯塔西奧・索莫薩・德拜萊於1967年掌權，並於1978年把總統職位交給同名兒子。陣線並非由一名將領遙控一切，而是依山區與城市設有區域指揮；反對派領袖維奧萊塔・查莫羅雖非野戰指揮者，卻在1979年的權力轉移中提供了政治支柱。
peopleEn: The Sandinista National Liberation Front was founded in 1961, with Carlos Fonseca, Silvio Mayorga, Tomás Borge, and Santos López forming its original core. Fonseca supplied political direction and guerrilla theory, Mayorga concentrated on organizing mountain columns, Borge tightened command and logistics, and Humberto Ortega, who joined later, became an important military commander. Edén Pastora joined in 1967; his previous service under General Sandino brought field experience different from that of the movement's student-background cadres. Fonseca was killed in combat in May 1968, while Mayorga died in a plane crash in December 1967, temporarily disrupting the early command structure. On the government side, Anastasio Somoza García ruled from 1936 until his assassination in 1956. After the brief presidency of Luis Somoza Debayle, Anastasio Somoza Debayle took power in 1967 and transferred the presidency to his son of the same name in 1978. The FSLN was not controlled by a single commander directing every operation; it maintained regional commands in mountain and urban areas. Opposition leader Violeta Chamorro was not a field commander, but she supplied political strength for the 1979 transition.
kits: 可由當時照片、繳獲紀錄及日後回憶核對的代表性武器，主要包括國民警衛隊的M1 Garand步槍、M1A1 Thompson衝鋒槍、M1 Browning Automatic Rifle、M1919A4 Browning輕機槍、M2 Browning重機槍，以及M1 60毫米與M1 81毫米迫擊砲。這些武器在1961年以前均已列裝。早期桑迪諾小組常從被襲擊的警衛據點取得同一批槍械，因此同一型號往往同時出現在政府軍與游擊隊手中，不能把雙方畫成完全隔絕的裝備體系。後期外來武器清單又見AK-47，其7.62×39毫米彈藥與美製.30-06及.45 ACP彈藥分開儲存，增加分配與補給難度。國民警衛隊另有AN/PRC-6系列手提無線電、GMC CCKW卡車與Willys MB越野車，憑空運與裝載量占優勢；桑迪諾方面則依靠徒步運輸、分散儲物與地方營地維持小單位。迫擊砲及配套瞄準具多集中於政府軍，後來被繳獲者才改變雙方的火力平衡。
kitsEn: Representative weapons verifiable through contemporary photographs, capture records, and later recollections included the National Guard's M1 Garand rifle, M1A1 Thompson submachine gun, M1 Browning Automatic Rifle, M1919A4 Browning light machine gun, M2 Browning heavy machine gun, and M1 60-millimeter and M1 81-millimeter mortars. All of these weapons had entered service before 1961. Early Sandinista teams frequently took the same weapons from attacked Guard posts, so the same models appeared on both government and guerrilla sides; the opposing forces cannot be represented as operating with completely separate inventories. AK-47 rifles also appeared in later external supply lists, and the separation of 7.62×39-millimeter ammunition from American .30-06 and .45 ACP stocks complicated distribution and resupply. The National Guard also had AN/PRC-6-series manpack radios, GMC CCKW trucks, and Willys MB jeeps, giving it advantages in radio coordination and carrying capacity. Sandinista units relied instead on movement on foot, dispersed storage, and local camps. Mortars and their aiming equipment were concentrated in government hands until captured weapons altered the balance of fire support.
tactics: 1961至1966年間，桑迪諾小組通常只有數人至十餘人，行動集中在中央山區的孤立警衛哨、巡邏隊與小型軍械庫。他們會在巡邏進入狹窄道路或山口時攻擊側翼，奪取武器、彈藥、無線電與糧食，然後在增援封閉道路前沿山徑撤往另一縣；遭遇封鎖時則分散成更小組，利用地形脫離接觸，不會為守住營地而進行漫長會戰。1967年底馬薩亞附近的Río Blanco行動遭到國民警衛隊追擊並蒙受重大損失後，陣線收縮核心、修正通信與撤退程序，並把零散游擊隊逐步整編為區域縱隊、營及指揮部。政府軍則依靠巡邏、封路與路障、車載機動縱隊、空中觀察及迫擊砲火力追查山區位置，再從縣級駐軍派出增援。1970年代，城市小組開始同步襲擊警察分遣所、通信站與政府機關，取得檔案和武器後迅速離開；1978至1979年的最後攻勢則把鄉村縱隊與城市突擊連接，使政府軍無法只靠封鎖一條山路便切斷所有行動。
tacticsEn: From 1961 through 1966, Sandinista teams commonly numbered from several men to slightly more than ten and concentrated on isolated Guard posts, patrols, and small depots in the central highlands. When a patrol entered a narrow road or mountain pass, the guerrillas would strike its flanks, seize weapons, ammunition, radios, and food, and withdraw along mountain trails before reinforcements could close the route. When surrounded, they broke into smaller groups and used the terrain to break contact rather than remaining in prolonged battles to hold a camp. After the National Guard pursued them at Río Blanco near Masaya in late 1967 and inflicted heavy losses, the FSLN tightened its core, revised communications and withdrawal procedures, and gradually reorganized scattered bands into regional columns, battalions, and command structures. Government forces relied on patrols, roadblocks and checkpoints, vehicle-mounted mobile columns, aerial observation, and mortar fire to locate mountain positions, followed by reinforcements from county garrisons. During the 1970s, urban teams began synchronized attacks on police stations, communications facilities, and government offices, taking documents and weapons before withdrawing. The final offensive of 1978 and 1979 then connected rural columns with urban attacks, preventing the government from severing every route by sealing a single mountain path.
data: 從1961年至1979年共跨18個日曆年；若按1967年公開內戰起算，則約為12年。可核對的時間骨架包括：1961年秋成立桑迪諾民族解放陣線；1964年前後把武裝鬥爭確定為主要道路；1967年12月底馬薩亞附近的Río Blanco行動遭重創；1968年5月方塞卡陣亡；1970年代初區域性游擊大隊與城市突擊逐步成形；1978年8月17日襲擊馬納瓜國家宮，9月16日發生馬薩亞列車事件；1979年春展開多路攻勢，最終在7月18日至19日完成政權崩解。兵力方面，1961年的活躍戰鬥者只有數十人，1970年代初增至數百人；1979年的常見概估把桑迪諾武裝及地方支援人員合計置於一萬至一萬五千之間，但這個數字不能全視為同質野戰兵。索莫薩方面的軍隊與國民警衛隊合計通常被概估為一萬以上、後期達數萬人，但不同來源對輔助武裝與警察的計算不一。Río Blanco及最後攻勢的傷亡數字在資料間差異很大，現有證據不足以支持一個可靠的總傷亡數，因此不列單一精確值。
dataEn: The period from 1961 to 1979 spans eighteen calendar years; counted from the commonly accepted beginning of the public civil war in 1967, it lasted about twelve years. The verifiable chronological framework includes the founding of the Sandinista National Liberation Front in the autumn of 1961; the decision around 1964 to make armed struggle the principal path; the disastrous Río Blanco action near Masaya in late December 1967; the death of Fonseca in May 1968; the formation of regional guerrilla battalions and urban commands during the early 1970s; the attack on the National Palace in Managua on 17 August 1978; the Masaya train action on 16 September; and the multi-axis offensive that culminated in the collapse of the regime on 18 and 19 July 1979. In terms of strength, the FSLN had only several dozen active fighters in 1961 and several hundred by the early 1970s. Common estimates for 1979 place its armed members and local support personnel between 10,000 and 15,000, although that figure cannot be treated as a homogeneous infantry force. Government forces, combining the army and National Guard, are generally estimated at more than 10,000 and eventually in the tens of thousands, but sources differ in their treatment of auxiliary armed personnel and police. Casualty figures for Río Blanco and the final offensive vary substantially between sources, and the surviving evidence does not support a reliable total; therefore no single precise casualty figure is given.
cause: 戰爭根源不是某一場突然爆發的單一事件，而是索莫薩家族統治、國家武力結構與反對力量長期形成的衝突。桑迪諾於1927至1933年抵抗美國干涉的歷史，以及1934年後流亡者保存下來的網路，為後來青年提供政治象徵；1959年古巴革命則使部分知識青年相信武裝奪權可以成功。索莫薩政府以家族成員輪替掌握總統職位，國民警衛隊享有遠高於普通軍隊的權力、武裝與司法特權，政治反對、工會活動與任何可能的選舉改革都受到嚴格控制。土地高度集中、進出口利益集中於少數家族，使體制衝突同時具有經濟與政治性質。FSLN內部雖有農民利益、民族主義、反獨裁及馬克思列寧主義等不同表述，各派對節奏與城市工作各有爭論，但推翻索莫薩統治是共同目標。1961年成立游擊組織並建立山區隊伍，才是能辨認的武裝衝突起點；此後外國援助、鎮壓強度與政治對立的互相推動，把原本有限的武裝鬥爭逐步變成全國性內戰。
causeEn: The war did not spring from a single sudden event. It grew from the interaction of Somoza family rule, the country's armed structure, and a steadily widening conflict with the opposition. Sandino's resistance to United States intervention from 1927 through 1933, and the networks preserved by exiles after 1934, provided later generations with a political symbol. The Cuban Revolution of 1959 convinced some educated young people that armed seizure of power could succeed. Under the Somoza government, members of the family succeeded one another as president, while the National Guard enjoyed authority, arms, and legal privilege far beyond that of the regular army. Political opposition, union activity, and even limited electoral reform were tightly restricted. Concentrated land ownership and control of export income by a small number of families made the conflict economic as well as political. Within the FSLN, formulations concerning peasant interests, nationalism, anti-dictatorship, and Marxism-Leninism differed, and factions disputed the tempo of struggle and the role of urban work, but overthrowing the Somoza regime was the shared objective. The establishment of a guerrilla organization and mountain columns in 1961 is the identifiable beginning of armed conflict. Subsequent foreign assistance, counterinsurgency, and political polarization then transformed a limited armed struggle into a nationwide civil war.
impact: 內戰把原本可以透過選舉、軍隊內部協商或反對黨聯合處理的衝突，變成由國民警衛隊與桑迪諾武裝組織直接較量的局面。政府擴大情報網、封路、臨時征用與集中兵力，並把被捕游擊者的處決、未經正常審判的懲罰及軍隊權力擴張制度化，進一步削弱其合法性；桑迪諾則從少數人游擊隊變成能在山區維持縱隊、在城市執行突擊並建立區域行政與政治組織的全國性力量。1978年1月3日，反對派人物兼前國民警衛隊將軍佩德羅・何塞・查莫羅遇刺，事件背後責任仍有爭議，但它消除了政府與反對派之間殘存的緩衝空間。同年美國國會因人權調查與制度風險而停止對索莫薩政府的軍事援助， OAS的壓力也同步增加。戰爭使交通、貿易與財政資源被長期 military deployment 吞噬，外國投資與合法出口信用下降，尼加拉瓜的國際孤立加劇。1979年以後，國家更替的結果把中美洲直接納入美蘇、古巴與美國支持的反對力量之間的冷戰衝突，而這是1961年成立游擊組織時所未能預見的長期後果。
impactEn: The civil war transformed a dispute that might otherwise have been handled through elections, negotiations inside the armed forces, or an opposition coalition into a direct contest between the National Guard and the Sandinista armed organization. The government expanded intelligence networks, road closures, temporary requisitions, and concentrated troop deployments. The execution of captured guerrillas, punishment without normal trial, and the expansion of military power became institutionalized, further damaging the regime's legitimacy. The Sandinistas, in turn, developed from a small guerrilla band into a nationwide force capable of maintaining mountain columns, conducting urban attacks, and building regional administrative and political organizations. On 3 January 1978, Pedro Joaquín Chamorro, an opposition leader and former National Guard general, was assassinated. Responsibility for the killing remains disputed, but the event removed what little space remained for mediation between the government and the opposition. During the same year, the United States Congress halted military assistance to the Somoza government after human-rights investigations and institutional-risk findings, while Organization of American States pressure also increased. The war diverted transport, trade, and fiscal resources into permanent military deployment, reduced foreign investment and legitimate export credit, and intensified Nicaragua's international isolation. After 1979, the resulting regime change drew Nicaragua directly into the Cold War confrontation among the Soviet Union, Cuba, and United States-supported counterforces, a long-term consequence not yet visible when the guerrilla organization was founded in 1961.
result: 1978年8月17日，桑迪諾突擊隊短暫進入馬納瓜國家宮，利用全國廣播發布公告、取得政府文件與武器後撤出；9月16日，又在馬薩亞線路上截停載有國民警衛隊人員及軍械的列車。這兩次行動不是立即奪取政權的終局，卻證明首都通信、交通與重要行政目標已能同時受到打擊。1979年春，陣線在馬薩亞、希諾特佩及北部山區展開多路攻勢，奪取城鎮、軍械庫與道路節點；國民警衛隊的指揮鏈因前沿單位被殲、倒戈、投降及中央失去控制而逐段崩解。7月18日，阿納斯塔西奧・索莫薩・德拜萊先到美國駐尼加拉瓜大使官邸，再經飛機離境；7月19日，索莫薩政府垮台，維奧萊塔・查莫羅、安德烈斯・卡斯特羅與莫伊塞斯・岡薩雷斯組成臨時政府接管國家。決定勝負的不是一場奪取馬納瓜的總攻，而是國家宮與馬薩亞行動造成的政治震動、1979年多戰區攻勢、國民警衛隊瓦解及政府失去維持秩序的能力。八月，新政府解散國民警衛隊並以桑迪諾人民解放軍取代其武裝職能。這樣的結果結束了索莫薩家族統治，也把1961年建立的山區游擊隊轉變成執政黨與全國軍隊，但政權轉移並不等於全國立即恢復穩定。
resultEn: On 17 August 1978, Sandinista commandos briefly entered the National Palace in Managua, used the national radio service to broadcast a communiqué, obtained government documents and weapons, and withdrew. On 16 September, they halted a train on the Masaya line carrying National Guard personnel and military materiel. Neither action immediately seized the government, but together they demonstrated that the capital's communications, transportation, and principal administrative targets could be struck at the same time. In the spring of 1979, the FSLN launched a multi-axis offensive across Masaya, Jinotepe, and the northern highlands, taking towns, depots, and road junctions. The Guard's chain of command broke down as forward units were destroyed, defected, surrendered, or lost contact with the center. On 18 July, Anastasio Somoza Debayle took refuge at the residence of the United States ambassador and then departed by aircraft. On 19 July, the Somoza government collapsed, and Violeta Chamorro, Andrés Castro, and Moisés González formed a provisional government to take control of the country. The outcome was not decided by a single assault on Managua. It resulted from the political shock created by the National Palace and Masaya actions, the multi-theater offensive of 1979, the disintegration of the National Guard, and the government's inability to preserve order. In August, the new government dissolved the National Guard and assigned its armed functions to the Sandinista People's Liberation Army. That result ended Somoza family rule and transformed the mountain guerrilla organization founded in 1961 into a governing party and national army, although the transfer of power did not bring immediate nationwide stability.
